Here's what I found (nothing changed — this is just the audit).

**Note on scope:** everything below lives in the `eval` memory space, not a project-specific space — worth confirming that's actually where you want atlas knowledge to live before handoff. There are ~120 live atlas claims total.

## Real duplicates (say the same thing twice)

- **"cargo nextest, not cargo test"** — stated twice, nearly verbatim:
  - *"Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used."*
  - *"The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test."*

- **"deploy via bin/ship.sh"** — stated three times with overlapping/redundant content:
  - *"Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root."* (most recently accessed)
  - *"To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo."* (same fact, stale — not accessed since Jul 23)
  - *"Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone."* (same fact plus one extra detail — the retired `make deploy` target)

## A real contradiction — worth resolving before handoff

Two claims about staging deploys directly conflict:
- *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically."*
- *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs bin/ship.sh --staging by hand."*

One of these is wrong (or the process changed and only one was updated). This matters for anyone picking up the project — worth pinning down which is current.

## Likely stale (flagged by the store itself as short-lived facts that overstayed)

- *"The branch under review is spike/consolidate."* — scratch/session-scoped, idle 40 days.
- *"The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api."* — "this week" was clearly a while ago; idle 40 days.

Both were filed with fast decay (i.e., meant to be temporary) but are still hanging around — good candidates to just let expire or explicitly forget.

## Worth a second look, not clearly wrong

- **"Feature flags"** appear to describe two different mechanisms under the same name: *"Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more"* (runtime flags, deleted a month after rollout) vs *"Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so cargo check --all-features has to pass"* (Cargo/compile-time feature flags). Not contradictory once you realize they're different systems, but easy for a new reader to conflate — might be worth renaming one of them for clarity.
- CI is described as running *"fmt, clippy, test and a no-default-features build"* in one claim, while another separately says *cargo check --all-features* has to pass — unclear if that's a step in the same pipeline or a separate one; the two claims don't fully reconcile.

Everything else that the similarity scan flagged (image registry vs. distroless base, Postgres 16 vs. rebuildable search index, connection-pool size vs. readiness probe, etc.) turned out to be distinct, non-conflicting facts that just share vocabulary — false positives, not real duplicates.

Want me to merge the duplicates, resolve the staging-deploy contradiction (once you tell me which is true), and let the two stale claims expire?
